chapter: Kid Rene, Chris Kelly and the bungalow
title: Best orchestras and the Scott Joplin repertoire
summary: He ranks Celestin, Desvignes, Maple Leaf, Robichaux and Tuxedo among the true orchestras.

story.theme_name: Who was in the band: naming sidemen and personnel
story.community_name: Who played in the band: reciting personnel

blocks.x: Yeah. But there ain't many. Outside of one band used to play that, I mean, I'm talking about band, I'm not talking about orchestra. It was Rene. Rene was more so near to that kind of stuff than any other band around there. But when they come down to playing the real orchestra, Scott Joplin, I'm a Sidney Desvene, Maple Leaf band, that was a known band, and the Tuxedo band. That was three known best bands around there. And the P. Ron's band.
But you say the other bands, they would play some of that. Yeah, yeah, yeah.

But I mean the real orchestras around here was Papa Celestan, Sidney Desvene, the Maple Leaf band, and John Rubenshut band. And the fourth best band around there. And Bob Lyon. You know what I mean? Bob Lyon is a pretty good band, but not in comparison with those fellas. How was Celestan on the trumpet? Was he a good musician? Well he was never no jazz trumpet player. He was a good musician, but he was never no jazz trumpet player. Good musician, but he was never no jazz trumpet player. When you remember the band in the old days, did they have shots with them? Or Ricard, Alexis, or do you know who the other trumpet players were? What did they do? Did one fellow play more of the solos and Celestan, just the regular orchestra part? Well I remember one time he had shots playing second trumpet. And he had Kid Ricard playing second trumpet too one time. But he mostly carried a seven piece band.
